mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in periods where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage growth and input costs, ultimately producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to margin pressure.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 5% for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).
